clue.text: Public pressure ensures that the soil is healthy

parts.note: the ground is the soil, so 'the soil is' reads as the ground's, contracted
well means in good health

explanation.surface: A gardener's slogan: keeping the soil in good condition guarantees results.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'the soil is healthy' as GROUND'S WELL and run it together; 'ensures that' only joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundswell is a growing tide of popular opinion that puts pressure on those in power.

clue.text: Acquired real estate in Swedish territory

parts.note: acquired means got
real estate is property in land

explanation.surface: Someone has bought property in Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: GOTLAND is the large Baltic island belonging to Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: Gotland is a Baltic island and province of Sweden.

clue.text: Sheepish appeal to a grape producer

parts.note: O is the vocative exclamation used when appealing to someone, as in 'O Lord'
a vine is the plant that bears grapes

explanation.surface: A shy, embarrassed plea addressed to a vineyard owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' looks like 'embarrassed', but it is meant literally: like a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine is the adjective for sheep, so 'sheepish' in its literal sense of sheep-like.

clue.text: Requires new wine-there's no other option

parts.note: requires means needs
must is grape juice that has just begun fermenting, i.e. new wine

explanation.surface: Someone insists a fresh wine is required, with no alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needs must' is the shortened proverb 'needs must when the devil drives': you do what circumstances force on you.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses compulsion, saying circumstances leave no alternative.

clue.text: A lot of players swagger

explanation.surface: A crowd of performers strutting about.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team of players; side also means pretentious airs, as in 'putting on side'.

clue.text: Grannie's made money

indicators.note: made in the sense of formed or constructed, so these letters are worked into something new

parts.note: the word grannies, with the apostrophe ignored, supplies all eight letters

explanation.surface: Grandmother has made a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges GRANNIES; the apostrophe is ignored, so its S counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the income or money someone takes in from work.

clue.text: Conservative consumed by the attraction of wealth

indicators.note: being consumed by something means being swallowed inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a lure is an attraction or enticement

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is swallowed up by the appeal of riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed by' puts C inside LURE; 'of' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or profit, usually with a disapproving flavour, as in 'filthy lucre'.

clue.text: Wrong opening to song leads to complaint

parts.note: mal- is a word beginning meaning badly or wrongly, as in malpractice
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: A badly begun song brings grumbles from the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' means an illness here, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can be an ailment, and malaria is a mosquito-borne disease.

clue.text: With permission Edward added yeast

parts.note: to have leave is to have permission, so being with permission is on leave
Ned is a pet form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward, having been allowed, put yeast in the dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Leavened dough has had a raising agent such as yeast worked into it.

clue.text: Concerned about top-class pupil with poor batting skills

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for concerned goes round the other pieces

parts.note: tender means caring or concerned
A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I
L is a learner, from the L-plate shown by learner drivers

explanation.surface: A caring teacher worries about a star pupil who cannot bat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the tail-ender comes in near the end of the batting order, being a poor batsman, usually a bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket term for a player batting at the end of the order, picked for skills other than run-scoring.

clue.text: About to being in fish from the basket

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about
to reel is to wind in a line and bring a caught fish ashore

explanation.surface: An angler is about to land a catch and pack it in the basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads like 'on the point of', but 'About' is C, for circa, and 'to bring in fish' is a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket in which anglers carry their catch.

clue.text: Disinclined to produce a piece of prose?

parts.note: a verse can be a numbered prose passage, as in a Bible verse, not only lines of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to write any prose at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the trick: a verse sounds like poetry, but a Bible verse is a short piece of prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means reluctant or opposed to something.

clue.text: Yield bowl

explanation.surface: An instruction to surrender a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To give over is to hand up or surrender; in cricket a bowler gives an over, six balls, when bowling.

clue.text: Do draw back and make yourself look glamorous

indicators.note: draw back is read as the word for draw turned backwards

parts.note: to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: Advice: pull yourself together and smarten up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw back' looks like 'retreat', but 'back' reverses PULL to give LLUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To doll yourself up is to dress and make up smartly to look attractive.

clue.text: Heather admits blasphemy causes disgust

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: ling is a common heather
an oath can be a profane curse or blasphemy

explanation.surface: Heather confesses swearing and causes revulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing is intense dislike or revulsion.

clue.text: I am no age to be destroyed by self-obsession

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked and broken up, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone protests they are not too old to be ruined by vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be destroyed' rearranges IAMNOAGE; 'by' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an obsessive preoccupation with oneself.

clue.text: Man keeps a receipt for ornamental stone

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the word for man contains the rest

parts.note: a man is a male
a chit is a note or receipt

explanation.surface: A man holds on to the receipt for a decorative stone he bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person doing the keeping, but it gives the letters that wrap round; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Malachite is a green copper mineral polished for jewellery and decorative carving.

clue.text: Exclude three articles made of fine cloth

parts.note: to bar is to exclude
a, the and a are three grammatical articles

explanation.surface: Leave out three items made from good fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' means items of clothing on the surface, but grammatical words A, THE, A in the parse.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine woollen fabric used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Hit the gin? Rubbish!

parts.note: to clap is to strike or slap
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: Someone hits the bottle, and someone else calls it nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is not the drink but an old word for a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense or empty talk.

clue.text: Defensive position results from unusual dialect

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so these letters are put out of their ordinary order

explanation.surface: A strange local speech produces a fortified stronghold.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress guarding a city, a stronghold for defence.

clue.text: Pleased to get directions to clearings in the wood

parts.note: pleased means glad
E and S are compass directions, east and south

explanation.surface: Happy walkers are given the way to open spaces in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Glades are open grassy spaces among trees in a forest.

clue.text: Sister holds large piece of fi needlework

indicators.note: holds means contains, so the abbreviation for sister goes around the other word

parts.note: ample means large or plentiful

explanation.surface: A nun clutches a big piece of embroidery.
explanation.walkthrough: Samplers were traditionally stitched by girls to show off their command of embroidery stitches.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampler is an embroidered cloth showing a range of stitches, often worked by girls as practice.

clue.text: Ah! To be embraced by a red-haired Pacific islander!

indicators.note: being embraced means being held within, so the exclamation goes inside the other word

parts.note: Titian describes a bright auburn red hair colour, after the painter
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at being hugged by a redhead from the South Seas.
explanation.walkthrough: TITIAN, the Venetian painter, gave his name to the auburn hair in his portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tahitian is a native of Tahiti, in French Polynesia in the South Pacific.

clue.text: Light displayed by church at the foot of a hill

indicators.note: in a down answer, the church being at the foot places it below the word for hill

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A lamp is shown by a church standing at the bottom of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable light, a flashlight or a flaming brand.

clue.text: Cry to go away around mid-September

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for go away goes about the middle letter

parts.note: scram means go away, clear off

indicators.note: mid picks out the central letter of the month's nine letters

explanation.surface: A shout telling someone to leave in the middle of September.
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud piercing cry.

clue.text: To practise extortion is perfectly correct

explanation.surface: Racketeering is apparently quite proper.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to extort payment or demand by force; exact also means precisely accurate.

clue.text: Malign a tradesman harbouring bloodsucker

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering inside, so the answer lies within these words

explanation.surface: Badmouthing a shopkeeper who shelters a parasite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbouring' points to the run of letters inside 'Malign a tradesman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small biting fly, some species of which suck blood.

clue.text: He gives the fellow an alternative

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A man offered another choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is a person who gives, such as money or blood.

clue.text: Dash to put up every roll of wallpaper!

definitions.text: to put up every roll of wallpaper

explanation.surface: A decorator exclaims in exasperation at hanging all the wallpaper rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Hang it all!' is an exclamation of annoyance like 'Dash it!'; literally it means paste up the whole lot.

clue.text: One quite fed up negotiating a treaty here

indicators.note: negotiating means working one's way through, so these letters are worked round into a new order

explanation.surface: A diplomat thoroughly sick of hammering out a treaty here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' looks like 'bored', but read literally it means filled with food.
explanation.definitionFit: A big eater who has plainly had plenty to eat is well filled, literally full up.
